property_summary: After depositing and attempting to collect, the sender's balance in Acc should have decreased by the amount collected, which fails when msg.value is replaced with 0.
After a successful Collect, the contract's ether balance decreases by exactly the amount collected.
After any call to Collect that reverts (due to insufficient balance), the msg.sender's Acc.balance must be unchanged from before the call.

After any sequence of operations that ends with a Collect call, the caller's Acc.balance can never exceed what they deposited (sum of msg.value in all Put calls) if the mutant's Put never adds balance.
After a successful Collect, the caller's Acc.balance is always less than or equal to the total ether they have sent to the contract via Put.
After calling Collect, the contract's ETH balance is unchanged (no net outflow), because balance changes only occur via sub_uint256 which reverts if balance < amount.
After any call to Collect, the mapping Acc[msg.sender].balance is non-decreasing relative to its value before the call.
After calling Collect, the balance of the caller's account in the contract should not decrease below its initial balance minus the requested amount.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the value of Acc[msg.sender].balance returned by the public getter is always at least its value before the call (i.e., balance never decreases).
After calling Collect, the caller's balance in the contract (Acc[caller].balance) should not have decreased compared to before the call.
For any account, after a successful Collect call, the balance of the account does not become zero if the account had sufficient balance before the call.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance is strictly less than the balance before the call.
After any successful Collect call, the caller's account balance in the contract is equal to the balance before the call minus the amount collected.
After a successful Collect call, the account balance in the contract is always greater than or equal to the amount collected if the unlock time has passed.
After a Collect call that reverts, the caller's balance in the contract remains unchanged.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum remains unchanged.
After any sequence of public calls ending in Collect(uint256), the contract's ether balance equals the sum of all account balances recorded in Acc mappings, regardless of reentrancy.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the unlock time for the caller is never decreased below the previous unlock time or the current block timestamp.
After a call to Collect(uint256), the sum of balances in Acc for all addresses that have ever interacted does not exceed the contract's ether balance.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), the calling address's balance strictly decreases by exactly the amount withdrawn when the withdrawal succeeds.
After collecting, the caller's balance in Acc must never be less than the amount withdrawn.

After calling Collect(uint256 _am), if the transaction does not revert, the caller's Acc balance must satisfy: original balance - collected amount = new balance, and the collected amount must be at least as large as _am (i.e., the full requested amount was sent).
After a successful Collect call, the caller's Acc balance must remain the same if the call did not revert, because the bug removal allows balance to decrease without the required check.
After Collect(uint256 _am), if the transaction does not revert, the caller's Acc balance must stay the same because the bug removes the acc.balance >= _am check, preventing any balance decrease.
After Collect(uint256 _am) succeeds, the caller's Acc balance must not decrease by more than _am.
After Collect, the balance of the caller never increases relative to its previous value.
After calling Collect, the caller's Acc balance does not increase beyond its previous value plus the amount withdrawn.
After calling Collect, the caller's Acc balance is never greater than its previous value.
After Collect, the sum of the caller's contract balance and their Acc balance does not change.
After Collect, the caller's Acc balance never increases relative to its previous value.
Collect should only succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the sender's unlockTime, ensuring that early withdrawal is not possible.
Collect must not revert when called with an amount equal to the balance and timestamp equals unlockTime.
Collect should never revert when the sender's balance equals the requested amount and the current timestamp is greater than the unlock time.
Collect should only succeed when block.timestamp is strictly greater than the sender's unlockTime.
Collect should revert when block.timestamp is strictly less than the unlock time, ensuring that funds cannot be withdrawn before the unlock time.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), the MinSum value is unchanged from its initial value
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint am), the MinSum value equals the constant set in the constructor, not the initial declaration.
After any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum equals the value set in the constructor (1 ether) regardless of the initial declaration.
MinSum is always equal to 1 ether after any sequence of public calls ending with Collect(uint256), because only the constructor sets it and no other function changes it.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect(uint256), MinSum equals the constant set in the constructor (1 ether).
